title: Getting started with mrpheus
text: mrpheus R package raw physiological signal analysis across biological rhythms research. ingests multi-modal physiological recordings — polysomnography (EDF/EDF+), MRI-concurrent physiological logs (Philips PMU), EEG — extracts features spanning three rhythm domains: cardiac (QRS detection, HRV), respiratory (apnoea detection, respiratory metrics), neural (spindles, slow oscillations, automatic AASM sleep staging). name spelled Morpheus carries silent m, pronounced Orpheus — carrying myths . title: Getting started with mrpheus
text: read_edf() wraps edfReader consistent output formatting: Pass only_header = TRUE inspect channels without loading signal data:
code: library(mrpheus)  rec <- read_edf("recordings/psg_001.edf") rec ## mrpheus EDF recording ## ℹ Path: recordings/psg_001.edf ## ℹ Duration: 7.98 hours ## ℹ Channels: 14 ## # A tibble: 14 × 3 ##   label              sample_rate transducer ##   <chr>                    <dbl> <chr> ## 1 EEG Fpz-Cz                 100 AgAgCl electrode ## 2 EEG Pz-Oz                  100 AgAgCl electrode ## 3 EOG horizontal              100 AgAgCl electrode ## ... hdr <- read_edf("recordings/psg_001.edf", only_header = TRUE)

title: Getting started with mrpheus
text: prepare_psg() segments recording 30-second epochs, classifies channels type (EEG, EOG, EMG, ECG, RESP), flags flat bad channels: Channel classification uses regex patterns can overridden:
code: psg <- prepare_psg(rec) psg ## mrpheus PSG ## ℹ Epochs: 958 × 30 s ## ℹ Recording: 7.98 h ## # A tibble: 14 × 4 ##   label              type  sample_rate   bad ##   <chr>              <chr>       <dbl> <lgl> ## 1 EEG Fpz-Cz         EEG           100 FALSE ## 2 EEG Pz-Oz          EEG           100 FALSE ## 3 EOG horizontal      EOG           100 FALSE ## ... psg <- prepare_psg(rec,   eeg_pattern  = "EEG|C3|C4|F3|F4|O1|O2|Fpz|Pz",   resp_pattern = "Thor|Abdo|Flow|SpO2|airflow" )

title: Getting started with mrpheus
text: detect_artifacts() flags epochs excessive amplitude high-frequency (muscle) contamination:
code: art <- detect_artifacts(psg) ## ℹ Artefact epochs: 12 / 958 (1.3%)

title: Getting started with mrpheus
text: compute_band_power() estimates PSD via Welch’s method integrates within standard EEG bands per epoch per channel: compute_spectrogram() returns time × frequency power matrix:
code: bp <- compute_band_power(psg, relative = TRUE) ## # A tibble: 958 × 9 ##   epoch channel    delta theta alpha sigma  beta gamma total_power ##   <int> <chr>      <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>       <dbl> ## 1     1 EEG Fpz-Cz 0.412 0.183 0.142 0.089 0.112 0.062          NA ## ... sg <- compute_spectrogram(psg, channel = "EEG Fpz-Cz", db = TRUE)

title: Getting started with mrpheus
code: sp <- compute_spindles(psg, channel = "EEG Fpz-Cz") so <- compute_slow_oscillations(psg, channel = "EEG Fpz-Cz")

title: Getting started with mrpheus
text: stage_epochs() stages epoch using pre-trained LightGBM model ported YASA (Vallat & Walker, 2021): Stages follow AASM nomenclature: W, N1, N2, N3, REM. Artefact epochs coded NA.
code: staging <- stage_epochs(   psg,   eeg_channel = "EEG Fpz-Cz",   eog_channel = "EOG horizontal",   emg_channel = "EMG chin",   artefacts   = art ) staging ## # A tibble: 958 × 7 ##   epoch stage prob_W prob_N1 prob_N2 prob_N3 prob_REM ##   <int> <chr>  <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl> ## 1     1 W      0.921   0.042   0.022   0.008    0.007 ## 2     2 W      0.874   0.081   0.031   0.007    0.007 ## 3     3 N1     0.312   0.448   0.185   0.032    0.023 ## ...

title: Getting started with mrpheus
code: hypnogram <- export_hypnogram(   staging,   epoch_s        = 30,   start_time     = rec$header$startTime,   participant_id = "P001" )  hypnor::plot_hypnogram(hypnogram) hypnor::compute_architecture(hypnogram)

title: Getting started with mrpheus
code: library(mrpheus)  rec      <- read_edf("recordings/psg_001.edf") psg      <- prepare_psg(rec) art      <- detect_artifacts(psg) bp       <- compute_band_power(psg, relative = TRUE) sp       <- compute_spindles(psg) so       <- compute_slow_oscillations(psg) staging  <- stage_epochs(psg, artefacts = art) hypnogram <- export_hypnogram(staging, start_time = rec$header$startTime)

title: Getting started with mrpheus
text: recordings acquired alongside fMRI, mrpheus reads Philips PMU .log files runs Pan-Tompkins QRS detection produce cardiac regressors. See vignette("mri-physiology") full workflow including scan-window alignment RR-per-TR computation.
code: # Read Philips PMU log (wBTU wireless VCG system, 496 Hz) rec <- read_philips_physlog("sub-01_ses-01_physlog.log")  # Detect QRS complexes qrs <- detect_qrs(as.double(rec$C[, "v1raw"]), fs = rec$HDR$sfreq)  # Instantaneous HR signal hr  <- compute_hr_signal(qrs)  # RR intervals per TR for BOLD regression rr_tr <- approx(   x      = qrs$qrs_i[-1] / rec$HDR$sfreq,   y      = diff(qrs$qrs_i) / rec$HDR$sfreq,   xout   = seq(0, n_vols * TR, by = TR),   method = "constant" )$y

title: MRI physiological signal processing
text: read_philips_physlog() parses Philips PMU .log file returns mrpheus_physlog object containing signal matrix, event markers, recording metadata. system argument sets hardware preset: resolved sampling frequency always rec$HDR$sfreq nothing downstream needs hardcode .
code: path <- system.file("extdata", "example_physlog.log", package = "mrpheus") rec  <- read_philips_physlog(path) rec #>  #> ── mrpheus Philips PMU recording ─────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ℹ Path: /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/mrpheus/extdata/example_physlog.log #> ℹ System: wBTU (496 Hz) #> ℹ Channels: v1raw, v2raw, v1, v2, ppu, resp, gx, gy, gz, mark #> ℹ Samples: 9920 (0.3 min) #> ℹ Markers: 52 events # Wireless VCG (Achieva/Ingenia dStream) — default rec <- read_philips_physlog(path, system = "wBTU")  # Older wired ECG system (500 Hz) rec <- read_philips_physlog(path, system = "wired")  # Site-specific sampling rate rec <- read_philips_physlog(path, system = "custom", sfreq = 400)

title: MRI physiological signal processing
text: wBTU layout provides ten channels:
code: # Signal matrix: samples x channels dim(rec$C) #> [1] 9920   10 colnames(rec$C) #>  [1] "v1raw" "v2raw" "v1"    "v2"    "ppu"   "resp"  "gx"    "gy"    "gz"    #> [10] "mark"  # Individual channels ecg  <- as.double(rec$C[, "v1raw"]) ppu  <- as.double(rec$C[, "ppu"]) resp <- as.double(rec$C[, "resp"])

title: MRI physiological signal processing
code: # Scanner timing rec$I$ScannerStart #> [1] 496 rec$I$ScannerStop #> [1] 9466  # ECG triggers logged by the scanner head(rec$I$VcgOnset) #> [1]  198  396  594  792  990 1188

title: MRI physiological signal processing
text: detect_qrs() implements Pan-Tompkins (1985) algorithm returns mrpheus_qrs object. R-peak indices qrs$qrs_i. Account qrs$delay need indices aligned raw (pre-filter) ECG.
code: qrs <- detect_qrs(ecg, fs = rec$HDR$sfreq) qrs #>  #> ── mrpheus QRS detection ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> ℹ R-peaks detected: 50 #> ℹ Mean HR: 150 bpm #> ℹ Filter delay: 37 samples (0.075 s) #> ℹ Sampling rate: 496 Hz # RR intervals (ms) rr_ms <- diff(qrs$qrs_i) / rec$HDR$sfreq * 1000 cat("Mean RR :", round(mean(rr_ms)), "ms\n") #> Mean RR : 399 ms cat("SDNN    :", round(sd(rr_ms)), "ms\n") #> SDNN    : 1 ms

title: MRI physiological signal processing
text: neonates, PPU often gives cleaner signal ECG electrodes. detect_qrs() accepts pulsatile channel:
code: qrs_ppu <- detect_qrs(as.double(rec$C[, "ppu"]), fs = rec$HDR$sfreq)

title: MRI physiological signal processing
text: compute_hr_signal() converts R-peak indices sample--sample instantaneous HR trace (bpm). reads fs mrpheus_qrs object directly:
code: hr <- compute_hr_signal(qrs) cat("HR range:", round(min(hr[hr > 0])), "–", round(max(hr)), "bpm\n") #> HR range: 150 – 151 bpm

title: MRI physiological signal processing
text: extract physiology aligned fMRI scan, use scanner-stop marker. reliable start marker exact recording onset varies stop always clean:
code: sfreq    <- rec$HDR$sfreq enddelay <- 42L       # samples between stop marker and scan end (site-specific) tr       <- 0.392     # fMRI TR in seconds vols     <- 47L       # number of volumes (adjusted for 20 s example)  stopidx  <- tail(rec$I$ScannerStop, 1L) - enddelay startidx <- stopidx - round(vols * tr * sfreq) startidx <- max(1L, startidx)  epoch <- rec$C[startidx:stopidx, ] cat("Epoch:", nrow(epoch), "samples /", round(nrow(epoch) / sfreq, 1), "s\n") #> Epoch: 9139 samples / 18.4 s

title: MRI physiological signal processing
text: rr_tr length-vols vector ready RETROICOR phase computation inclusion nuisance regressor GLM.
code: qrs_epoch <- detect_qrs(as.double(epoch[, "v1raw"]), fs = sfreq)  rr_t <- qrs_epoch$qrs_i[-1] / sfreq rr_s <- diff(qrs_epoch$qrs_i) / sfreq  tr_times <- seq(0, vols * tr, by = tr) rr_tr    <- approx(rr_t, rr_s, xout = tr_times, method = "constant")$y  cat("RR per TR (first 5):", round(rr_tr[1:5] * 1000), "ms\n") #> RR per TR (first 5): NA NA 399 399 399 ms

title: MRI physiological signal processing
code: library(mrpheus)  # 1. Read rec <- read_philips_physlog("sub-01_ses-01_physlog.log")  # 2. Extract scan epoch sfreq    <- rec$HDR$sfreq stopidx  <- tail(rec$I$ScannerStop, 1L) - 42L startidx <- stopidx - round(2300L * 0.392 * sfreq) epoch    <- rec$C[startidx:stopidx, ]  # 3. QRS detection qrs <- detect_qrs(as.double(epoch[, "v1raw"]), fs = sfreq)  # 4. HR signal hr <- compute_hr_signal(qrs)  # 5. RR per TR for BOLD regression rr_tr <- approx(   x      = qrs$qrs_i[-1] / sfreq,   y      = diff(qrs$qrs_i) / sfreq,   xout   = seq(0, 2300 * 0.392, by = 0.392),   method = "constant" )$y

title: mrpheus — Physiological signal analysis for biological rhythms research
text: mrpheus raw signal layer Circadia Lab R ecosystem. ingests processes multi-modal physiological recordings — polysomnography (EDF/EDF+), MRI-concurrent physiological logs (Philips PMU), EEG — extracting features across biological rhythms connect sleep, cardiac function, neural activity. package covers three rhythm domains: cardiac (QRS detection, HRV), respiratory (apnoea detection, respiratory metrics), neural (spindles, slow oscillations, automatic AASM sleep staging). Staged hypnograms pass downstream hypnor; derived metrics pass syncR. name spelled Morpheus carries silent m, pronounced Orpheus — portmanteau myths simultaneously. title: Detect QRS Complexes in an ECG Signal (Pan-Tompkins Algorithm) — detect_qrs
text: Detects R-peaks raw ECG signal using Pan-Tompkins algorithm. Implements bandpass filtering, derivative, squaring, moving-average integration, adaptive dual-threshold peak detection T-wave rejection search-back missed beats.

title: Detect QRS Complexes in an ECG Signal (Pan-Tompkins Algorithm) — detect_qrs
text: ecg Numeric vector. Raw ECG signal. fs Numeric. Sampling frequency Hz. ecg comes read_philips_physlog(), use rec$HDR$sfreq.

title: Detect QRS Complexes in an ECG Signal (Pan-Tompkins Algorithm) — detect_qrs
text: list class mrpheus_qrs components: qrs_i Integer vector R-peak sample indices (1-based), referenced bandpass-filtered signal. qrs_amp Numeric vector R-wave amplitudes detected peak (normalised bandpass signal units). delay Numeric. Sample delay introduced moving-average stage (half 150 ms window length). fs Numeric. Sampling frequency passed function.

title: Detect QRS Complexes in an ECG Signal (Pan-Tompkins Algorithm) — detect_qrs
text: Processing pipeline (Pan & Tompkins, 1985): Bandpass filter 5–15 Hz (Butterworth N=3). fs = 200 Hz, implemented separate 12 Hz low-pass 5 Hz high-pass stages. Derivative filter — 5-point kernel interpolated match fs. Squaring — non-linear emphasis dominant peaks. 150 ms moving-average integration. Adaptive thresholding — dual-threshold scheme T-wave rejection search-back missed beats (initialised 2-second training window). R-peak indices returned relative bandpass-filtered signal. Account delay need indices aligned raw ECG.

title: Detect QRS Complexes in an ECG Signal (Pan-Tompkins Algorithm) — detect_qrs
text: Pan J, Tompkins WJ. real-time QRS detection algorithm. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng. 1985;32(3):230–236. doi:10.1109/TBME.1985.325532

title: Detect QRS Complexes in an ECG Signal (Pan-Tompkins Algorithm) — detect_qrs

what: mrpheus: Raw Physiological Signal Analysis for Biological Rhythms Research — mrpheus-package
title: mrpheus: Raw Physiological Signal Analysis for Biological Rhythms Research — mrpheus-package
text: Raw physiological signal analysis biological rhythms research. Provides ingestion, artefact detection, event detection, feature extraction multi-modal physiological recordings including polysomnography (EDF/EDF+), MRI-concurrent physiological logs (Philips PMU), EEG. Covers cardiac rhythm (QRS detection, HRV), respiratory rhythm (apnoea detection, respiratory indices), neural oscillations (sleep spindles, slow oscillations, automatic AASM sleep staging via pre-trained LightGBM model ported YASA; Vallat & Walker, 2021). Exports staged hypnograms hypnor derived metrics syncR. Part Circadia Lab R ecosystem Northumbria University.

title: Read a Philips MRI Physiological Log File — read_philips_physlog
text: path Character. Path Philips .log file. system Philips PMU hardware preset. One : "wBTU" (default) Wireless VCG system, 496 Hz. 10-channel layout: v1raw, v2raw, v1, v2, ppu, resp, gx, gy, gz, mark. Used Philips Achieva/Ingenia dStream wireless body telemetry unit. "wired" Older wired ECG system, 500 Hz. Fewer channels (accelerometer); layout read file header. "custom" Supply sfreq explicitly. sfreq Numeric NULL. Sampling frequency Hz. Overrides system preset supplied. Required system = "custom". channels Character vector NULL. Channel names return. NULL (default) returns channels. "none" returns signal data (markers ). skipprep Logical. TRUE, skip samples recorded blank # line marks end preparation phase. Default FALSE.

text: list class mrpheus_physlog components: C Integer matrix (samples × channels). Column order matches file header. M Two-column integer matrix: marker (bit-encoded value) index (1-based sample number) every non-zero marker. Named list 1-based sample index vectors event type: VcgOnset, PpuOnset, TriggerResp, Measurement, ScannerStart, ScannerStop, TriggerExt, Calibration, RefTriggerVcg. HDR List header metadata: ID, DATETIME, STATS, DockableTable, COLUMN_NAMES, system, sfreq. path Character. Resolved path source file.

title: Read a Philips MRI Physiological Log File — read_philips_physlog
text: Bit-encoded marker values:   Use scanner-stop marker (reliable start) time-lock data:
code: 0x0001  ECG trigger       0x0002  PPU trigger      0x0004  respiration 0x0008  slice onset       0x0010  scanner start    0x0020  scanner stop 0x0040  external trigger  0x0080  calibration      0x8000  ref ECG trigger stopidx  <- tail(data$I$ScannerStop, 1) - enddelay startidx <- stopidx - round(n_vols * TR * data$HDR$sfreq) epoch    <- data$C[startidx:stopidx, ]

text: Initial release. Package scaffolded full PSG analysis pipeline. read_edf() / prepare_psg() — EDF/EDF+ ingestion, channel inventory, epoch segmentation, bad-channel flagging. detect_artifacts() — amplitude high-frequency artefact detection. compute_band_power() — Welch PSD δ/θ/α/σ/β/γ bands per epoch. compute_spectrogram() — STFT-based time-frequency spectrogram. compute_spindles() — RMS envelope spindle detection (Lacourse et al., 2019). compute_slow_oscillations() — zero-crossing detection (Mölle et al., 2002). stage_epochs() — automatic AASM staging via pre-trained LightGBM model ported YASA (Vallat & Walker, 2021). Feature extraction parity Python pipeline progress. export_hypnogram() — returns mrpheus_hypnogram object ready hypnor::new_hypnogram() hypnor available. detect_apneas(), compute_ahi(), compute_odi() — respiratory stubs, full implementation pending. compute_hrv_sleep() — HRV stub, full implementation pending. palette_orpheus — 8-colour palette extracted Roman mosaic Orpheus Charming Animals (3rd century AD, Palermo Archaeological Museum).
